case_title.quote: RAMESH AND OTHERS v. STATE OF HARYANA
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment caption.

number_of_accused.quote: convicting all the four accused persons (appellants herein)
number_of_accused.reason: Judgment consistently refers to four accused.

accused_gender.correct_value: Male and Female (Ramesh and Suresh male; Saroj and Prem female)
accused_gender.quote: Saroj (wife of Suresh) and Prem (mother in law)
accused_gender.reason: Value omits the female co-accused Saroj and Prem.

accused_age.reason: No age is given for any accused in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of accused is not mentioned.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of accused is not mentioned.

accused_occupation.reason: Occupation is not stated; only a truck is mentioned in the statement under s.313.

previous_criminal_record.reason: No criminal record is stated; only s.107/151 Cr.P.C. proceedings are mentioned.

victim_gender.quote: Smt. Roshni, wife of Appellant no. 1
victim_gender.reason: Victim is female, referred to as Smt. Roshni.

victim_age.reason: Victim's age is not stated; only marriage duration and children's ages are given.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Husband (Ramesh); in-laws (Suresh brother-in-law, Saroj sister-in-law, Prem mother-in-law)
accused_victim_relationship.quote: my husband Ramesh came and Suresh his brother, i.e., my devar
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Value captures only spouse; other accused were in-laws of the victim.

offence_category.reason: Headnote classifies the case as dowry death.

statutory_provisions.correct_value: IPC ss.302, 34, 498-A; also CrPC s.378 (appeal against acquittal) and s.313, s.161 references
statutory_provisions.reason: IPC sections are correct, but the CrPC s.378 appeal provision central to the judgment is omitted.

weapon.quote: Ramesh sprinkled kerosene on her. Suresh lighted a matchstick
weapon.reason: Kerosene is the weapon/means described in the dying declaration and facts.

evidence_type.correct_value: Dying declaration; medical (doctor's fitness certificate, MLR, post-mortem); oral testimony of witnesses; recovery; site plan
evidence_type.quote: PW-11 ... proved the same as Ex. PH/3
evidence_type.reason: Omits oral witness testimony (PW-3, PW-4, PW-11) and site plan evidence.

confession.reason: No confession is described; the disclosure statement is not treated as a confession.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: No aggravating circumstances are expressly identified as such.

trial_court_outcome.quote: The appellants herein were tried and acquitted by the Sessions Court

high_court_outcome.quote: the High Court, in appeal, has overturned the verdict of acquittal, thereby convicting all the four accused
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court convicted all four accused.

final_outcome.quote: We, thus, do not find any merit in this appeal, which is accordingly dismissed.
final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, leaving the conviction in place.

offence_finally_established.quote: Section 302/34 IPC:- To undergo rigorous imprisonment for life
offence_finally_established.reason: Conviction under s.302 IPC (murder) with s.34 is upheld.

imprisonment_type.quote: To undergo rigorous imprisonment for life
imprisonment_type.reason: Main sentence is rigorous imprisonment for life.

imprisonment_years.reason: Main sentence is life, so no fixed term; the 2-year term under s.498-A is ancillary.

fine_rs.quote: to pay a fine of Rs. 10,000/-
fine_rs.reason: Fine of Rs. 10,000 under s.302/34 matches the judgment.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Facts only, without stating the court outcomes; the husband and his brother (not the victim's brother) allegedly set her on fire
neutral_facts.quote: the High Court, in appeal, has overturned the verdict of acquittal
neutral_facts.reason: Facts reveal the trial, High Court and Supreme Court outcomes; also wrongly calls the attacker the victim's brother.

offence_severity.quote: rigorous imprisonment for two years and to pay a fine of Rs.2,000/-
offence_severity.reason: Sentences listed match the High Court sentence order.

attempt_completion.quote: Roshni succumbed to injuries within few hours
attempt_completion.reason: Offence was completed; the victim died.

physical_harm.quote: it was found that she was suffering from 100% burns

number_of_offences.correct_value: Two offences charged: s.302/34 and s.498-A/34 IPC; four accused
number_of_offences.quote: tried and acquitted by the Sessions Court for offences under Sections 302, 34, 498A
number_of_offences.reason: Value describes accused count, not offences; two offence heads were charged.

financial_property_loss.reason: No financial or property loss is discussed; treated as not stated.

premeditation_planning.reason: Premeditation or planning is not discussed.

motive.correct_value: Continuous dowry demands and harassment by husband and in-laws
motive.quote: The deceased was being harassed by her husband and in-laws on continuous demand of dowry
motive.reason: Value merely restates the offence category rather than the motive of dowry demands.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the doctor found that she was in a conscious state of mind and was competent to give her statement
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Dying declaration before Magistrate with doctor's fitness certificate was accepted as stated.

witness_credibility.quote: appears to have been won over by the appellants
witness_credibility.reason: PW-4 found influenced by accused and his testimony false per PGIMS records.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Accused Ramesh, Suresh and Prem took the victim to PGIMS hospital; trial court considered this conduct
post_offence_conduct.quote: The trial court also took into consideration the conduct of other appellants... who had taken the deceased to the hospital
post_offence_conduct.reason: Judgment discusses accused taking victim to hospital, which the trial court treated as conduct evidence.

trial_duration.quote: The trial court acquitted the appellants herein
trial_duration.reason: Value gives appellate outcomes, not trial duration, which the judgment does not state.

legal_representation.quote: Praveen Kr. Aggai-Wal, Upendra Pratap Singh, San jay Jain, Advs. for the Appellants

investigation_status.quote: a report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. was presented before the Court of Jurisdictional Magistrate
investigation_status.reason: FIR registered, police report filed, and trial completed as described.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Trial court gave no weight to doctor's fitness opinion, gave no reasons for disbelieving the Magistrate, and overlooked hospital records
procedural_irregularity.quote: Admittedly, no weightage is given by the trial court to the opinion of the Doctor
procedural_irregularity.reason: Judgment identifies several procedural and appreciation errors by the trial court.

appeal_history.quote: the High Court, in appeal, has overturned the verdict of acquittal
appeal_history.reason: Acquittal, High Court conviction and Supreme Court dismissal of appeal are correctly sequenced.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: Respondent argued the victim gave the statement after reaching hospital, authorities found her fit, and there was no reason to discard it; supported High Court
prosecution_argument.quote: there was no reason to discard the statement as was wrongly done by the trial court
prosecution_argument.reason: Core argument matches, but 'legally unsustainable' is the Court's finding, not the respondent's argument.

defence_argument.quote: under no circumstances could she be in a position to give the statement
defence_argument.reason: Defence argued 100% burns made statement incapable and relied on Ramesh being with PW-4.

legal_principle_applied.correct_value: Dying declaration before Magistrate with doctor's fitness certificate is admissible despite burn extent; appellate interference in acquittal limited to perversity/substantial reasons
legal_principle_applied.quote: this dying declaration cannot be discarded merely going by the extent of burns
legal_principle_applied.reason: Omits the appellate-interference principle on acquittal, which the Court discussed at length.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Sanwat Singh v. State of Rajasthan 1961 SCR (3) 120 - relied on
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Listed precedents match those relied upon in the judgment.

sentencing_rationale.reason: Judgment does not discuss sentencing rationale or deterrence; the sentence is simply reproduced from the High Court.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: No mitigating factors are discussed in the judgment.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: No aggravating factors are discussed for sentencing.

other_sentence_order.quote: In default of payment of fine, to further undergo rigorous imprisonment for one year.
other_sentence_order.reason: Only default-imprisonment terms appear, which are part of the sentence order itself.
